insider_note: x¹⁸ is (x⁹)², not a fresh power to fear — spotting that 18 is double 9 is the one observation that turns this into a plain Tan⁻¹ question.

page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: Substitute t = x⁹
steps.why: Recognising x¹⁸ as (x⁹)² makes the denominator 1+t² for t=x⁹, and the leftover x⁸dx is exactly (1/9)dt since d/dx(x⁹)=9x⁸.
common_mistakes: Not spotting that x¹⁸=(x⁹)², and trying some other substitution that does not simplify the denominator to 1+t².
Forgetting the 1/9 that comes from dividing by the 9 in d(x⁹)=9x⁸dx.
steps.memory_tip: 18 = 2×9, so x¹⁸ = (x⁹)² — always check whether a high power is really a lower power, squared.

steps.label: Integrate and back-substitute for the final answer
steps.why: (1/9)∫dt/(1+t²) = (1/9)Tan⁻¹t + c is the standard Tan⁻¹ formula with a=1, and substituting t=x⁹ back in completes the answer.
common_mistakes: Forgetting the outside factor of 1/9 in the final answer.
Forgetting to substitute x⁹ back in for t.
steps.memory_tip: The 1/9 picked up from the substitution survives to the very end — it is not absorbed into anything else.
